one_line: bibliometric index measuring patient involvement in how research is produced
skills: composite index construction from text signals
data: PubMed (E-utilities: titles, abstracts, author lists, affiliations, acknowledgements, grant metadata)
NIH iCite (Relative Citation Ratio, control sample)
ClinicalTrials.gov / AACT (explorer app and PFDD layer)

decisions.chose: retrieving the corpus on patient-involvement keyword terms, chunked by publication year
decisions.over: building the corpus around a disease or set of diseases
decisions.because: the object of study is a mode of production rather than a condition, and year chunking keeps the retrieval from favoring recent work
decisions.evidence: The corpus is retrieved on 13 patient-involvement keyword terms, chunked by publication year to avoid recency bias.

decisions.chose: three separately constructed control sets (stratified random, journal-matched, MeSH-heading-matched)
decisions.over: one comparison against a random sample
decisions.because: a single random comparison leaves journal and disease area confounded with the exposure
decisions.evidence: A single comparison against a random sample would leave the effect confounded with journal and disease area.

decisions.chose: coarsened exact matching on year bin and team size bin
decisions.because: it matches the identification strategy of the benchmark paper and bounds imbalance up front instead of checking balance afterwards
decisions.evidence: because CEM bounds imbalance ex ante instead of requiring post-hoc balance checking (Iacus, King & Porro, 2012)

decisions.chose: Relative Citation Ratio as the outcome
decisions.because: RCR normalizes each paper to a field baseline built from its own co-citation network, so fields with different citation cultures stay comparable
decisions.evidence: Relative Citation Ratio normalizes to a field baseline built from each paper's own co-citation network (Hutchins et al., 2016)

decisions.chose: false-discovery-rate correction on the per-heading tests only
decisions.over: correcting the primary comparison as well
decisions.because: the primary comparison is pre-specified while the per-heading tests are a multiple-testing family
decisions.evidence: The primary comparison is pre-specified, so it takes no correction.

broke.what: a case-folding bug: the scorer lowercased the text but kept capitalized patterns, so every acronym-based signal could never fire
broke.evidence: `score_signals` lowercased the text, then searched with patterns containing capitals.

broke.what: substring matching on organization names produced false hits on unrelated institutions
broke.evidence: Grant and affiliation matching lowercased both sides and used `in`, so "nord" hit Novo Nordisk, Helse Nord, Nordic, "Avenue Nord".

broke.what: the collective-author signal was tagging research consortia and outcome-measurement groups as patient collectives, which mislabeled a headline signal in the draft
broke.evidence: Its keyword list includes "consortium" and "community", so it catches research consortia

broke.what: once patterns became case-insensitive, a bare sample-size notation started matching results-section text and tagging unrelated studies as self-experimentation
broke.evidence: bare `N=1` matched sample counts in results sections ("(n=1) withdrew")

broke.what: a figure and its signal table disagree because they came from different pipeline runs, and the repo lists reconciling them to one canonical run as open
broke.evidence: This is a snapshot difference between two pipeline runs and needs reconciling to one canonical run before submission.

question: Can patient involvement in how research gets produced be measured from published papers, and does involved research differ from comparable research without it?
rejected_line: Wanted involvement scored from each paper's funding-statement text; the corpus carries PubMed grant lists only, so OpenAlex funder metadata stood in.
